examples.en: I dip the acorn jelly in seasoned sauce and eat it.
After hiking, I ate seasoned acorn jelly.
They say acorn jelly is low in calories, so it's good for dieting.

examples.ko: 저기요, 도토리묵 한 접시랑 파전 주세요.
examples.en: Excuse me, one plate of acorn jelly and a scallion pancake, please.
My grandmother made acorn jelly herself for us.

examples.ko: 차가운 도토리묵이 여름에 입맛을 살려 줘요.
examples.en: Cold acorn jelly revives your appetite in summer.

explain: 도토리 가루로 만든 묵이에요. 청포묵, 메밀묵처럼 재료에 따라 이름이 달라요. 묵은 '만들다'보다 '쑤다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: The seasoned dotorimuk is tangy and tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 묵을 양념에 버무려 만든 반찬 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the side dish made by mixing the jelly with seasoning.

phrases.en: My grandmother made dotorimuk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 묵은 '만들다'보다 '쑤다'를 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For jellies like muk, 'ssuda' is more common than 'make'.

phrases.en: I cut the dotorimuk into bite-size pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹기 전에 묵을 자르는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes cutting the jelly before eating.

explain_en: It is a jelly made from acorn starch. Like 청포묵 and 메밀묵, its name changes depending on the ingredient. For making muk, people often say '쑤다' rather than '만들다'.

examples.ko: 이 커피는 뒷맛은 깔끔한데 향이 약해요.
examples.en: This coffee has a clean aftertaste, but the aroma is weak.
I drank water to get rid of the bitter aftertaste.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 결말이 슬퍼서 뒷맛이 씁쓸했어요.
examples.en: The movie's ending was sad, so it left a bitter aftertaste.
It's a fruit that leaves a slight sourness in the aftertaste.

examples.ko: 이 차는 처음엔 떫지만 뒷맛도 부드러워요.
examples.en: This tea is astringent at first, but the aftertaste is smooth too.

examples.ko: 싸운 뒤에는 늘 뒷맛이 개운치 않아요.
examples.en: After a fight, it always leaves an uneasy feeling.

explain: 음식을 먹거나 마신 뒤에 입에 남는 맛이에요. '뒷맛이 깔끔하다/쓰다/달다'처럼 말해요. 어떤 일이 끝난 뒤 남는 기분도 '뒷맛이 씁쓸하다', '뒷맛이 개운치 않다'처럼 비유로 써요.

phrases.example: 이 차는 뒷맛이 깔끔해서 자주 마셔요.
phrases.en: This tea has a clean aftertaste, so I drink it often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹고 난 뒤 입에 맛이 남지 않아 좋다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment: nothing unpleasant lingers in the mouth after eating.

phrases.en: Even though we won, it left a bitter aftertaste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 끝난 뒤 기분이 개운하지 않을 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Figurative use for a feeling that is uneasy after something ends.

phrases.en: The spicy aftertaste lingers for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛이 입에 계속 있다는 뜻으로, 앞에 어떤 맛인지 같이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the taste stays in your mouth; say what taste it is before it.

explain_en: It is the taste left in the mouth after eating or drinking, as in '뒷맛이 깔끔하다/쓰다/달다'. It is also used figuratively for the feeling left after an event, as in '뒷맛이 씁쓸하다' or '뒷맛이 개운치 않다'.

en: to be soft; to be tender; to be squishy

examples.en: Please have some soft, ripe persimmons.
This jelly is soft, so it's easy to eat.
The bread is still soft, so eat it quickly.

examples.ko: 반죽이 말랑한 정도가 되면 모양을 만드세요.
examples.en: When the dough becomes soft, shape it.

examples.ko: 떡이 굳기 전에는 말랑했는데 지금은 딱딱해요.
examples.en: The rice cake was soft before it hardened, but now it's hard.
I like the texture that is soft yet chewy.

explain: 눌렀을 때 탄력 있게 부드러운 느낌이고, 반대말은 '딱딱하다'예요. '물렁하다'와 모음만 다른 짝이고 '말랑말랑'으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Freshly baked soft bread is delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사가 올 때 '말랑한'으로 바꿔서 부드러운 음식이나 물건을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun it becomes '말랑한', describing soft food or objects.

phrases.en: This doll feels squishy when you touch it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말랑말랑'으로 반복하면 부드러운 느낌이 더 살아나요.
phrases.nuance_en: Repeating it as 말랑말랑 brings out the soft feeling more.

phrases.en: This fruit isn't soft yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 덜 익어 단단하다는 뜻을 부정형으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, saying something is still firm or unripe.

explain_en: Spoken, springy softness you can press, like bread or jelly. It describes something springy and pleasantly soft when pressed, and the opposite is '딱딱하다' (hard). It is a vowel-variant partner of '물렁하다' and is also often used as '말랑말랑'.

t90.ax: When the dough becomes soft, shape it.

examples.en: I season the meat with salt and pepper beforehand.
Put the pre-seasoned chicken in the refrigerator.
I seasoned the fish before grilling it.
If you don't season it first, it tastes bland.
Season it first, then wait ten minutes.
My mother seasons the vegetables first before mixing them.

explain: 요리를 본격적으로 하기 전에 재료에 먼저 간을 해 두는 일이에요. 요리하면서 나중에 간을 맞추는 건 '간을 맞추다'라고 해요. 명사 '밑간'을 써서 '밑간을 하다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: Season the fish with salt beforehand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 '밑간하다'를 명사 '밑간'으로 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb '밑간하다' spelled out with the noun '밑간'.

phrases.en: If you season it in advance, it's tastier.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 두다'를 붙여 미리 준비해 둔다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 두다' means doing it in advance.

phrases.en: After seasoning, wait about ten minutes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리 순서를 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when explaining the steps of a recipe.

explain_en: It means lightly seasoning the ingredients before the main cooking begins. Adjusting the taste later while cooking is '간을 맞추다'. You can also use the noun and say '밑간을 하다'.

examples.ko: 이 빵에는 방부제가 들어 있지 않아요.
examples.en: This bread has no preservatives in it.
I want to eat food without preservatives.
Without preservatives, a lunch box spoils quickly.

examples.ko: 방부제를 많이 쓰면 건강에 안 좋다고 해요.
examples.en: They say using a lot of preservatives is bad for your health.
Check the ingredients that are used as preservatives.
A little preservative goes into cosmetics too.

explain: 음식이 상하지 않게 넣는 물질로, 화장품에도 쓰여요. 일상에서는 '방부제'라고 하고, 식품 성분표에서는 '보존료'라는 말도 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: No preservatives were added to this bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 만들 때 방부제를 더한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means adding preservatives when making food.

phrases.en: This cosmetic has no preservatives.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식뿐 아니라 화장품에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used for cosmetics as well as food.

phrases.en: I check whether the snack contains preservatives.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제품 안에 방부제가 있는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say whether a product contains preservatives.

explain_en: It is a substance added to keep food from spoiling, and it is used in cosmetics too. In daily talk people say '방부제', and on food ingredient labels you may also see the term '보존료'.

examples.en: Silkworm pupae smell distinctive, but they taste good.
They sell silkworm pupae in paper cups on the street.
A caterpillar becomes a pupa and then turns into a butterfly.
Silkworm pupa soup tastes even better in winter.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 학교 앞에서 번데기를 사 먹었어요.
examples.en: When I was little I bought and ate silkworm pupae in front of school.
I observed a pupa attached to a leaf.

explain: 곤충의 번데기를 가리키기도 하고, 삶은 누에 번데기로 만든 길거리 간식을 가리키기도 해요. 간식은 냄새 때문에 호불호가 갈려요. 속담에서도 가끔 나와요.

phrases.example: 요리사 앞에서 요리법을 가르치다니 번데기 앞에서 주름 잡는 격이에요.
phrases.en: Teaching a chef how to cook is like showing off in front of an expert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 아는 사람 앞에서 아는 척하며 나서는 것을 놀리듯 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said teasingly when someone shows off in front of a person who knows far more.
phrases.en_equiv: teach your grandmother to suck eggs

explain_en: It means the pupa stage of an insect and also the street snack made of boiled silkworm pupae. The snack divides people because of its smell. It also appears occasionally in proverbs.

examples.ko: 복어는 독이 있어서 아무나 요리하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Pufferfish is poisonous, so not just anyone may cook it.
At the aquarium, the pufferfish swelled up like a balloon.
My father likes pufferfish soup.

examples.ko: 복어를 잡으면 바로 바다에 놓아 줘야 해요.
examples.en: If you catch a pufferfish, you should put it back in the sea right away.
Pufferfish dishes are a bit expensive.

examples.ko: 저는 복어 사진을 찍으려고 아침 일찍 갔어요.
examples.en: I went early in the morning to take a photo of a pufferfish.

explain: '복어'는 독이 있어서 면허가 있는 요리사만 다룰 수 있어요. 한국에서는 맑은 국으로 먹는 '복어 지리'가 유명해요. 몸이 부풀어 오르는 모습으로 그림책에도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I ate pufferfish soup to cure my hangover.
phrases.nuance_ko: 복어를 넣은 맑은 국이에요. 한국에서 복어를 먹는 대표적인 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A clear soup made with pufferfish, a typical way of eating it in Korea.

phrases.en: Pufferfish dishes are a bit expensive but tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 복어로 만든 음식 전체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to dishes made from pufferfish in general.

phrases.example: 복어 독은 아주 위험해서 조심해야 해요.
phrases.en: Pufferfish poison is very dangerous, so you must be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 복어가 가진 독을 말해요. 그래서 면허가 있는 요리사만 요리할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The poison that pufferfish carry, which is why only licensed chefs can cook it.

explain_en: '복어' is poisonous, so only licensed chefs can prepare it. In Korea it is best known as the clear soup '복어 지리'. Its habit of puffing up also makes it a common picture-book animal.

examples.en: Please put a lot of lettuce in my hamburger.
Lettuce stays crisp if you wash it and drain the water.
I put lettuce and tomatoes in the salad.

examples.ko: 양상추가 너무 비싸서 오늘은 다른 채소를 샀어요.
examples.en: Lettuce was too expensive, so I bought other vegetables today.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 양상추 반 통이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: There's half a head of lettuce left in the fridge.

examples.ko: 양상추로 쌈을 싸 먹으면 고기가 덜 느끼해요.
examples.en: Wrapping meat in lettuce makes it feel less greasy.

explain: 둥글고 속이 단단한 양상추는 샌드위치, 햄버거, 샐러드에 많이 넣어요. 고기를 싸 먹는 부드러운 잎채소는 보통 '상추'라고 해서 서로 구분해요.

phrases.en: I had a lettuce salad for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양상추를 먹는 가장 흔한 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to eat lettuce.

phrases.en: I bought a head of lettuce at the mart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둥근 채소는 '한 통'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Round vegetables like this are counted as 한 통.

phrases.en: Please chop the lettuce into small pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cooking.

explain_en: Round, firm-hearted 양상추 goes into sandwiches, burgers and salads. The soft leafy kind used to wrap meat is usually called '상추', so Koreans tell the two apart.

t90.ax: I put lettuce and tomatoes in the salad.

examples.en: In summer, cold noodles are at their best.
Kimchi only gets its true taste once it is well fermented.

examples.ko: 이 집 떡볶이는 매워야 제맛을 느낄 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only get the real flavor of this place's tteokbokki when it is spicy.

examples.ko: 땀 흘린 뒤에 마시는 물이 제맛인 걸 알아요?
examples.en: Do you know that water tastes best after you sweat?

examples.ko: 제맛은 역시 직접 담근 김치에서 나와요.
examples.en: The real flavor comes from kimchi you made yourself.
Isn't this exactly the real thing?

explain: 'N이 제맛이다'는 어떤 음식이나 일이 가장 좋을 때, 또는 그렇게 해야 진짜 맛이 난다고 말하는 표현이에요. 음식뿐 아니라 '운동은 새벽에 해야 제맛이다'처럼 즐거움에도 써요. 발음은 [제맏]이에요.

phrases.en: Ramen tastes right only when it's cooked in a pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 방법으로 해야 진짜 맛이 난다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say something tastes right only when done a certain way.

phrases.en: Pajeon is the best on a rainy day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 좋은 때와 음식을 짝지어 '이게 최고예요'라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs the best time with a food to say 'this is the best way to enjoy it.'
phrases.en_equiv: ~ is the real deal / the best

phrases.example: 직접 만들어 먹어야 제맛을 느낄 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can only get the real taste by making it yourself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 일의 진짜 즐거움을 느낀다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means feeling the real enjoyment of food or an activity.

explain_en: 'N이 제맛이다' says that something is at its best or that you only get the real enjoyment in that way. It is not only for food; you can say '운동은 새벽에 해야 제맛이다' for other pleasures too. It is pronounced [제맏].

examples.en: Fermented skate is famous as a strong-smelling food.
In Jeolla, people eat skate at feasts.

examples.ko: 처음 먹은 홍어는 코가 아플 정도로 독했어요.
examples.en: The first skate I ate was so strong it made my nose sting.
I bought a skate at the market.

examples.ko: 돼지고기, 묵은 김치와 같이 먹는 홍어삼합이 유명해요.
examples.en: Hongeo samhap, skate eaten with pork and aged kimchi, is famous.

examples.ko: 삭힌 홍어는 좋아하는 사람과 싫어하는 사람이 갈려요.
examples.en: Opinions on fermented skate split between lovers and haters.

explain: 삭혀서 먹는 요리로 유명해서 한국 사람들 사이에서도 좋아하는 사람과 싫어하는 사람이 확실히 갈려요. 홍어, 돼지고기, 묵은 김치를 함께 먹는 '홍어삼합'이 대표적이에요. 생선 이름이지만 음식 이야기에서 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: Hongeo samhap has a strong smell the first time you eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 홍어, 돼지고기, 묵은 김치를 함께 먹는 대표 요리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The signature dish of skate, pork, and aged kimchi eaten together.

phrases.en: I tried skate with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식으로 먹는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about eating it as food.

phrases.example: 삭힌 홍어는 코가 아플 정도로 냄새가 강해요.
phrases.en: Fermented skate smells so strong it stings your nose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 홍어 요리의 특징을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain what makes the dish distinctive.

explain_en: It is famous as a fermented dish, and even Koreans split sharply between lovers and haters. The classic way is '홍어삼합': skate with pork and aged kimchi. It is a fish name, but it comes up more in food talk.

en: a bold heart; nerves of steel

examples.ko: 저는 강심장이 아니라서 발표할 때 떨려요.
examples.en: I don't have strong nerves, so I get nervous when I present.

examples.ko: 혼자 귀신의 집에 들어가다니 정말 강심장이네요.
examples.en: Going into a haunted house alone, you're really fearless.
He has nerves of steel, so he didn't tremble even in the interview.

examples.ko: 강심장인 사람만 번지 점프를 할 수 있대요.
examples.en: They say only people with strong nerves can bungee jump.

examples.ko: 강심장을 가진 선수라서 마지막 순간에도 침착했어요.
examples.en: As a player with nerves of steel, he stayed calm even at the last moment.
You slept soundly the night before the exam? You have nerves of steel.

explain: 겁이 없고 담이 큰 사람을 말해요. 칭찬일 때도 있고, 놀랍다는 뜻으로 가볍게 말할 때도 있어요. 반대로 쉽게 겁먹고 긴장하는 사람은 '소심하다'나 '새가슴'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I envy people with nerves of steel who can smile even in an interview.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강심장을 사람 앞에 붙여 '겁 없는 사람'이라고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to describe a person who is fearless.
phrases.en_equiv: a person with nerves of steel

phrases.en: Going on a trip alone, you're really bold.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강심장'과 비슷한 뜻의 관용 표현이고, 놀라거나 감탄할 때 말로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An idiom close in meaning to 강심장, often used in speech to express surprise or admiration.

phrases.example: 저는 강심장이 아니라서 큰 소리에도 놀라요.
phrases.en: I'm not tough, so even loud noises startle me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겁이 많고 쉽게 긴장하는 자기 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are timid and get nervous easily.

explain_en: It describes someone who is fearless and bold. It can be praise, or a light remark of surprise. The opposite, someone who gets scared or nervous easily, is called '소심하다' or '새가슴'.

en: to be winding; to be crooked; to be tightly curvy

examples.en: The mountain road is winding, so please go slowly.
The baby's hair is curly.
If you follow the winding alley, you'll find a cafe.
The ramen noodles are curled up in squiggles.
The road isn't winding, so it's easy to drive.
The child drew a squiggly line on the paper.

explain: '구불구불'과 비슷해서 길, 머리카락, 선에 다 쓸 수 있어요. '꼬불꼬불'은 작게 여러 번 꺾이는 느낌으로 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: We went up along the winding road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, change it to the '-ㄴ' form to describe it.

phrases.en: The ramen noodles are curly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양이 작게 여러 번 꺾였다고 말할 때 쓰는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form for saying something has many small twists and curves.

phrases.en: I drew a wiggly line on the paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-하다' 없이 부사처럼 써서 동작을 꾸며 줄 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Without '-하다', it works like an adverb describing an action.

explain_en: It is similar to '구불구불' and can describe roads, hair or lines. '꼬불꼬불' often gives the feeling of many small bends.

examples.ko: 아이는 부끄럼이 많아서 말을 잘 못 해요.
examples.en: The child is shy, so he can't speak up easily.
My face turned red from shyness.

examples.ko: 그는 부끄럼 없이 큰 소리로 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: He sang loudly without any embarrassment.

examples.ko: 부끄럼이 많은 아이도 친해지면 말이 많아져요.
examples.en: Even a shy child talks a lot once they get close.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 사람 앞에서는 부끄럼이 생겨요.
examples.en: I get bashful in front of people I meet for the first time.

examples.ko: 거울 앞에서 연습하면서 부끄럼을 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: I overcame my shyness by practicing in front of a mirror.

explain: '부끄럼'은 성격으로 쉽게 쑥스러워하는 마음에 많이 써서 '부끄럼이 많다'가 자주 짝이 돼요. 잘못해서 느끼는 창피한 마음은 '부끄러움'이 더 자연스러워요. 한 단어로 비슷한 '수줍음'은 낯선 사람 앞에서 조용해지는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 동생은 낯선 사람 앞에서 부끄럼을 잘 타요.
phrases.en: My younger brother gets shy in front of strangers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉽게 쑥스러워하는 성격을 말할 때 쓰는 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural collocation for describing a person who is easily shy.

phrases.en: I felt ashamed after I made a mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못해서 창피한 마음에는 '부끄럼'보다 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For the embarrassed feeling after doing something wrong, this is more natural than 'bukkeureom'.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 수줍음이 많아서 처음엔 말을 안 해요.
phrases.en: That friend is very shy, so he doesn't talk at first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낯선 사람 앞에서 조용해지는 마음에 써서 '부끄럼'과 가까워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to 'bukkeureom', used for going quiet in front of unfamiliar people.

explain_en: 부끄럼 is used for a shy personality that is easily embarrassed, so 부끄럼이 많다 is a common pairing. The feeling of shame after doing something wrong is more naturally 부끄러움. The similar 수줍음 is the feeling of going quiet in front of strangers.
